definition.def: If you refer to the scale of something, you are referring to its size or extent, especially when it is very big.
examples: However, he underestimates the scale of the problem. [+ of]
You may feel dwarfed by the sheer scale of the place.
The break-down of law and order could result in killing on a massive scale.
The British aid programme is small in scale.

definition.def: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.
examples: ...an earthquake measuring five-point-five on the Richter scale.
The patient rates the therapies on a scale of zero to ten.
The higher up the social scale they are, the more the men have to lose.

definition.def: A pay scale or scale of fees is a list that shows how much someone should be paid, depending, for example, on their age or what work they do. [British]
examples: ...those on the high end of the pay scale.
A Registered Osteopath will be pleased to tell you his scale of fees before you decide on a consultation.

definition.def: The scale of a map, plan, or model is the relationship between the size of something in the map, plan, or model and its size in the real world.
examples: The map, on a scale of 1:10,000, shows over 5,000 individual paths. [+ of]

definition.def: A scale model or scale replica of a building or object is a model of it which is smaller than the real thing but has all the same parts and features.
examples: Franklin made his mother an intricately detailed scale model of the house.

definition.def: In music, a scale is a fixed sequence of musical notes, each one higher than the next, which begins at a particular note.
examples: ...the scale of C major. [+ of]

definition.def: The scales of a fish or reptile are the small, flat pieces of hard skin that cover its body.
Scales are a piece of equipment used for weighing things, for example for weighing amounts of food that you need in order to make a particular meal.
examples: ...a pair of kitchen scales.
...bathroom scales.
I step on the scales practically every morning.

definition.def: If you scale something such as a mountain or a wall, you climb up it or over it. [written]
examples: ...the first British woman to scale the world's highest mountain. [VERB noun]
The men scaled a wall and climbed down scaffolding on the other side. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If something is out of scale with the things near it, it is too big or too small in relation to them.
examples: The tower was surmounted by an enormous statue, utterly out of scale with the building. [+ with]

definition.def: If the different parts of a map, drawing, or model are to scale, they are the right size in relation to each other.
examples: ...a miniature garden, with little pagodas and bridges all to scale.

definition.def: To scale back means the same as to scale down. [mainly US]
examples: Despite current price advantage, U.K. manufacturers are still having to scale back production. [VERB PARTICLE noun]

definition.def: If you scale down something, you make it smaller in size, amount, or extent than it used to be.
examples: One factory has had to scale down its workforce from six hundred to only six. [VERB PARTICLE noun]
The air rescue operation has now been scaled down. [VERB PARTICLE noun (not pronoun)]
The Romanian government yesterday unveiled a new, scaled-down security force. [VERB-ed PARTICLE]

definition.def: If you scale up something, you make it greater in size, amount, or extent than it used to be.
examples: Simply scaling up a size 10 garment often leads to disaster. [VERB PARTICLE noun (not pronoun)]
Since then, Wellcome has been scaling up production to prepare for clinical trials. [VERB PARTICLE noun]
